source: DPROD Contracts dprod-contracts/examples/baseline.ttl, policy <https://example.org/agreements/trading-market-data-2026> (EKGF dprod, develop, 50db943)
needs: profile conflict default (odrl:conflict odrl:prohibit on the DPROD profile)
notes: The bilateral twin of dprod-market-data-feed: the same offer's rules as an accepted Agreement, with the two duties referenced by IRI (duty:mkt-*-2026-001) as in the source and the anonymous rules named rule:tm-*. ex:conformTo is declared odrl:includedIn odrl:use, which the source omits and ODRL IM §2.4 requires (decisions/0034, EKGF/dprod#286); without it the vendored source is rejected with InvalidActionHierarchy. The duty nodes' dprod:dutyState triples are dropped (due2 derives status; exception 2). Both duties name the trading team as subjectOfDuty — grantorDuties in DPROD; the grantee has no duty here, so the bilateral partition is one-sided. Every rule names analytics as assignee, so a grantor request is NotApplicable in both systems (the exception-4 divergence needs a subject-less rule; dprod-divergences covers it). DPROD duty collection (§7.2 step 1): deliver and conformTo never match display or nonDisplay, so no duty is collected and no violation denies. Intended §7.4 reading throughout; DPROD Σ assumed produced from the same evidence where scenarios supply it.

scenarios.name: analytics displays the feed, one interval missed

expected.why: rule:tm-display applies (assignee analytics, display) and the distribute prohibition does not match display: Permit. The delivery instances are as in dprod-market-data-feed scenario 5 — the 09:00 delivery at 09:02 fulfils the first, the 09:15 and 09:30 intervals are violated — and the missed intervals are reported and cost nothing (§6.1). The schema obligation is in force and outstanding.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (no duty collected for a display; the permission is active for the grantee)

expected.why: ex:nonDisplay matches rule:tm-non-display by equality and assignee, and its constraint holds (internal): Permit. The distribute prohibition does not match nonDisplay. The delivery duty's anchor defaults to effective_at 09:40, and an INTERVAL rule generates its anchor, so one instance is owed at 09:40 with its five-minute window open: outstanding. The schema obligation is in force and outstanding.
rule:tm-no-distribute matches by equality and assignee: Deny. The schema obligation remains in force — a Forbid of the policy matches the request.

scenarios.name: the grantor displays under its own contract

expected.why: Every rule names analytics as assignee; the trading team is the assigner, and no party closure makes it below analytics. Nothing matches: NotApplicable, and no obligation is in force. DPROD agrees — the agreement is applicable for either party (§7.3), but no norm is active for the grantor (§7.4).

scenarios.dprod_expected: NotApplicable (applicable agreement, but every norm names the grantee)
